title: Investigation and health risk assessment of PM2.5 during potato and meat frying
author: Qasemi, Alami, et al.

steps.title: Prepare laboratory environment
steps.instruction: Close all windows and doors, turn off mechanical ventilation, hoods, and exhaust fans; verify that room air temperature is between 21.5 °C and 23.4 °C; use a natural‑gas‑powered stove (gas supplied from the distribution system) and a cooker as the heat source; conduct the experiment in the chemistry laboratory of Gonabad University of Medical Sciences, Gonabad, Iran.

steps.title: Set sampling geometry
steps.instruction: Position the PM2.5 sampling inlet 1.20 m above the floor and 30 cm horizontally from the gas stove, corresponding to the height of the human respiratory zone.

steps.title: Select food and oil
steps.instruction: Choose the test food (potato slices or veal meat pieces) and the oil type: (a) sunflower oil alone (non‑frying oil) or (b) a frying oil mixture of sunflower oil + canola oil; employ the deep‑frying method for all trials.

steps.title: Heat pan and oil
steps.instruction: Place a pan on the stove, heat it, add the selected oil, and continue heating the oil until it reaches the target frying temperature of 150 °C, 190 °C, or 240 °C.

steps.title: Fry food and sample air
steps.instruction: Transfer the chosen food (potato or meat) into the hot oil; simultaneously start air sampling using a set of sorbent tubes and filters for the entire frying period.

steps.title: Repeat experiments
steps.instruction: Perform each combination of food (2), oil type (2), and temperature (3) three times, resulting in a total of 144 air samples (2 foods × 2 oils × 3 temperatures × 3 replicates).

steps.title: Analyze PM2.5 samples
steps.instruction: Analyze the collected sorbent tubes and filters with the Particulate Air Monitoring Equipment (HAZ‑DUST Model EPAM‑5000, USA) to determine PM2.5 concentrations.
